data.headline: Target group
data.text: Because the scientific disciplines of Computer Science and Automation Engineering come together in a large area of overlap to form a uniform field of knowledge, the Master's degree in Automation & IT aims to both expand and deepen students' knowledge of the subject and methods in this field. By further developing their social and individual skills, the students are prepared for employment in positions of responsibility in research, development, project planning, production, and management.

data.headline: Admission requirements
data.text:
A relevant Diplom or Bachelor's degree from a university of applied sciences or university specialising in Engineering Sciences or Computer Science and an overall grade of at least 'good' (grade up to 2.5).

Applicants must present their motivation for the Master's course in detail in a letter of motivation of approx. two pages in English. The letter of motivation is used to determine the applicant's aptitude for the course. Applications without a letter of motivation will not be considered.

The determination of course-related aptitude is based on the final grade attained in the previous degree, the specialist focus of the previous degree and the letter of motivation.

data.text: Usability, User Experience, User Research, Usability Testing, Digital Production for Interaction Design, Psychology for UX Practitioners, Strategic Usability Engineering, Human Computer Interaction (HCI), Methodology, Interaction Design

data.headline: Admission requirements
data.text: The formal admission requirements for the Master's degree course in Usability Engineering conducted in English are: a professionally qualifying certificate of academic degree degree (BSc) in a relevant degree course; at least 210 ECTS points or ideally a total study time of 7 standard full-time semesters (graduates with a Bachelor's degree with less than 210 ECTS points can meet the admission requirements by catching up on defined modules). Any semesters completed to prepare for the main course of study cannot be recognised; evidence of sufficient English language proficiency (at least level C1 according to the Common European Framework of Reference (CEFR) or equivalent, unless the professionally qualifying certificate of academic degree was already in English). Please note that the requirement for the successful completion of this Master's degree course is a total study volume of 300 ECTS credits.

data.headline: Annotation
data.text:
We support you personally and continuously in achieving your goals. Based on our proven CORE principle, we have coordinated all learning objectives, forms of examination as well as teaching and learning methods for you in such a way that learning is fun and you will achieve the best possible learning success.

Digital teaching and learning content
The use of digital elements in teaching is an essential component of our teaching and learning concept. Whether in virtual group rooms, chats with lecturers or in mobile learning apps, with us, you will be optimally prepared for the demands of the modern working world. You will get to know a variety of digital tools and methods that are precisely tailored to the skills that will help you in your studies and later career. Communication platforms such as MS Teams or Zoom are integrated into your everyday study routine as a matter of course.

Internationality
The SRH University of Applied Sciences Heidelberg maintains a broad network of partnerships around the world to enable you to spend time studying abroad: In a semester abroad, an internship or in a summer school, you can gain unique experiences worldwide, which will bring you unforgettable experiences with lifelong friendships.

data.headline: Admission requirements
data.text:
Admission to this Master's degree programme at SRH University is open to those who meet the following requirements:
• Internationally recognised Bachelor's course degree (180 ECTS) or a German diploma degree in Computer Science or in the subjects of "Virtual Realities", "Applied Computer Science", "Information Management", IT, Software Development or comparable degrees
• Good knowledge of object-oriented programming languages (Java/C++/Python etc.) as well as databases (MySQL, PostgreSQL or Oracle)
• Evidence of English language proficiency: IELTS 6.5 / TOEFL 80 / Duolingo Certificate 95 / PTE Academics 58 or equivalent tests

Heidelberg: EU/EEA (incl. Western Balkans, Switzerland and Ukraine): EUR 840/month, non-EU/EEA: EUR 6,950/semester

Munich: EU/EEA (incl. Western Balkans, Switzerland, Ukraine): EUR 840/month, non-EU/EEA: EUR 5,750.00/semester

Stuttgart: EU/EEA (incl. Western Balkans, Switzerland, Ukraine): EUR 840/month, non-EU/EEA: EUR 5,750/semester


A one-off registration fee of EUR 750 (EU/EEA)/ EUR 1,000 (non-EU/EEA) will be charged.

data.headline: Target group
data.text: The course is aimed at graduates of Bachelor's degree courses at universities and universities of applied sciences, and graduates of courses leading to a Diplom at a university of applied science. It is aimed at German students with an interest in an internationally-oriented course of study as well as international students with an interest in later employment in Germany.

data.headline: Annotation
data.text:
Pre-application process:

The Course Management offers an application pre-check of the relevant documents (Bachelor's degree, Bachelor's transcript, language certificate) for determination of eligibility according to our examination regulations. We start with the pre-check in April. These documents can be sent in one merged PDF file with a maximum size of 16348KB/16MB to

service-esm@fh-dortmund.de

Cooperation course with the Bochum University of Applied Sciences and the Westphalian University of Applied Sciences.

data.headline: Admission requirements
data.text: Bachelor of Science or Bachelor of Engineering (three or four years), 'Diplom-Ingenieur' (engineer) in Computer Science, Business Computing, Information Technology, Software Engineering, or equivalent with a final grade or mark of at least 'good' (2.5). It must be evident that previous studies included a thesis. The previous studies have to include sufficient knowledge in the relevant fields of software engineering and digital systems.

data.headline: Focus
data.text: Data Management, Big Data, Data Protection, Data Analytics, Research and Ethics, Software Engineering & Programming (Full-Time)

data.headline: Target group
data.text: The course is geared to the needs of working people. The courses/lectures are bundled and usually take place at weekends, supplemented with online coaching.

data.headline: Annotation
data.text:
We support you personally and continuously in achieving your goals. Based on our proven CORE principle, we have coordinated all learning objectives, forms of examination as well as teaching and learning methods for you in such a way that learning is fun and you will achieve the best possible learning success.

Digital teaching and learning content
The use of digital elements in teaching is an essential component of our teaching and learning concept. Whether in virtual group rooms, chats with lecturers or in mobile learning apps, with us, you will be optimally prepared for the demands of the modern working world. You will get to know a variety of digital tools and methods that are precisely tailored to the skills that will help you in your studies and later career. Communication platforms such as MS Teams or Zoom are integrated into your everyday study routine as a matter of course.

Internationality
The SRH University of Applied Sciences Heidelberg maintains a broad network of partnerships around the world to enable you to spend time studying abroad: In a semester abroad, an internship or in a summer school, you can gain unique experiences worldwide, which will bring you unforgettable experiences with lifelong friendships.

data.headline: Admission requirements
data.text:
To apply for the Bachelor’s degree programme in Ergotherapy, you will need:

- Bachelor’s degree with 180 ECTS in Computer Science, Business Informatics or a related field and at least one year of qualified and relevant professional experience in one of the areas of IT, Marketing, Logistics, Production or Finance.
- Proof of English language skills: IELTS 6.5 / TOEFL 80 / Duolingo Certificate 95 / PTE Academics 58 or equivalent tests
A one-off enrolment fee of EUR 750 will be charged at the beginning of the course.

data.headline: Focus
data.text: Cyber Security, Information Security, Information Security, IT Security, Computer Science, Business Informatics, Data Analysis, Data Analysis, Data Security, Safety

data.headline: Target group
data.text:
Graduates with a Bachelor in natural sciences, engineering and computer science.
Alternatively, also graduates with a Bachelor who have a keen interest in IT security and have advanced skills in mathematics and statistics.

data.headline: Annotation
data.text:
Our degree course trains you to become a cyber security specialist who has profound IT knowledge and who can plan and implement information security systems and measures in companies and other institutions.

You will deal with current topics such as blockchain, DevSecOps and cryptocurrencies and receive comprehensive training in the field of information security. In addition to specialised knowledge in security technologies, IT security management and data analysis, you are just as familiar with operational processes and organisational theory as you are with the legal challenges in data protection.

data.headline: Admission requirements
data.text:
To apply for the Master's degree programme in Computer Science - Cyber Security, you will need:

- University or university of applied sciences degree (Bachelor’s or Diploma degree) in computer science and related disciplines
– Letter of motivation
- Certificate of general or subject-specific higher education entrance qualification
- Proof of command of English
- Curriculum vitae with current passport photo
- Copy of identity document (front and back), copy of passport or national identity card for foreign students

data.headline: Target group
data.text: Graduates of Computer Science and Natural Sciences with sufficient Mathematics and Statistics skills

data.headline: Annotation
data.text:
Our degree program offers you a computer science education that includes classical modules such as software development and programming, but also provides specialised knowledge in the field of Big Data and Artificial Intelligence.

You learn about the latest big data technologies and how to implement AI and machine learning tools in companies and the business environment. In addition to technological expertise, the practice-oriented curriculum helps you to specialise your analytical, business and soft skills in various projects and internships.

data.headline: Admission requirements
data.text:
To apply for the Master’s degree programme in Computer Science – Big Data and Artificial Intelligence, you will need:

- University or university of applied sciences degree (Bachelor’s or Diploma degree) in computer science and related disciplines
– Letter of motivation
- Certificate of general or subject-specific higher education entrance qualification
- Proof of command of English
- Curriculum vitae with current passport photo
- Copy of identity document (front and back), copy of passport or national identity card for foreign students

- Ideally 210 ECTS, but at least 180 ECTS. For the Bachelor with 180 ECTS, individual agreements are made before the start of the course in order to achieve the missing ECTS.

Recognition may be granted if the qualifications are relevant and the applicant has at least three years of relevant professional experience.

data.headline: Focus
data.text: Data Science, Phyton, Academic Work, Statistics, SQL, Cloud Computing, Neural networks and deep learning

data.headline: Annotation
data.text: Progressing digitisation is causing data volumes to grow immeasurably. A topic that has long since become a matter of public debate. Therefore, data experts who approach the developments in the areas of software and infrastructure engineering as well as big data technologies with solution skills in a methodical, targeted and consistent way are desperately sought-after. With a distance learning Master's degree in Data Science at the IU, you will ensure that you have optimum career opportunities on the labour market. And: you study 100% online, how, when and where you want.

data.headline: Admission requirements
data.text:
You have completed an apprenticeship or further education, work experience or have already studied? Then let your previous achievements be recognized for the correspondence course! This way you save time as well as tuition fees - namely EUR 30 per recognized ECTS point.
\t
- Shortening your study time: Skip individual modules or entire semesters!
- Save on tuition: For every ECTS point you get you save EUR 30.

We will be happy to check before your application for distance learning whether and to what extent we can take your previous achievements into account: noncommittally and 100% online. Simply fill out our online recognition form.

data.headline: Annotation
data.text: Computer Science is a subject area that is changing rapidly, is at the cutting edge of our age and has become the pacemaker for the digital society of the future. In the English-language IU Master's degree programme in Computer Science, you will focus on Data Science, Cybersecurity and Artificial Intelligence. Due to the unmet need for experts on these topics, you will become a sought-after specialist who can work in almost all industries. Your Master's degree course provides you with all the necessary skills to establish yourself as a specialist on the international labour market.

data.headline: Admission requirements
data.text:
You have completed an apprenticeship or further education, work experience or have already studied? Then let your previous achievements be recognized for the correspondence course! This way you save time as well as tuition fees - namely EUR 30 per recognized ECTS point.
\t
- Shortening your study time: Skip individual modules or entire semesters!
- Save on tuition: For every ECTS point you get you save EUR 30.

We will be happy to check before your application for distance learning whether and to what extent we can take your previous achievements into account: noncommittally and 100% online. Simply fill out our online recognition form.

data.headline: Focus
data.text: Data Analytics, Change Management, Process Management, Innovation Management, Leadership, Digital Transformation, Digital Transformation, Cyber Security, Company Development

data.headline: Annotation
data.text:
Our Master’s degree course MSc Digital Transformation Management offers you a modern, digital business education with a technological focus.

You will learn how to best support companies in their digital transformation and how to involve relevant stakeholders. You will learn about the special features of digital business models and the power that disruptive innovations can have. You will learn about various methods for generating ideas and how digital change can be promoted in companies.

The modules on innovation management, change management and process management will strengthen your expertise, as will the integration of current topics such as strategic management, organisational development, intercultural management and diversity.

Thanks to the degree course’s focus on skills and projects, you will enhance your communication, conflict resolution and teamwork skills and become versed in agile project management and coaching methods.

Your semester abroad will also help you broaden your horizons as you will spend a semester at a partner university or doing a work placement.

data.headline: Admission requirements
data.text:
You will need:
- Degree from a university or university of applied sciences (Bachelor's or Diploma degree) in economics, computer science, business informatics and related disciplines
OR
- Degree from a university or university of applied sciences in another field + 6 months relevant professional training
– Letter of motivation
- Proof of English language proficiency
- Certificate of general or subject-specific higher education entrance qualification
- C.V.
- Copy of ID

data.headline: Admission requirements
data.text:
Successful completion of a university degree in a relevant degree course with a minimum final qualification of Bachelor with an overall grade of at least 2.5, as well as compliance with the additional admission requirements listed below.

A degree course is relevant if it contains at least 80 ECTS credits in computer science or information science content.
Further information on the application process and the template for listing the required ECTS can be found at www.digital-sciences.de.

The degree of relevance of the Bachelor's degree is determined depending on the chosen field of study.

An application is already possible if you have not yet completed your degree course, but are expected to complete them before the start of the Master's degree programme.

modules.name: DAAD Hochschulkompass

data.headline: Annotation
data.text:
Creating Ideas to Shape our Future

Digital innovations are the core of new business models, the founding of start-ups and the strategy of all companies that want to enhance their future viability and competitiveness. We study new work, agile methods and ways of thinking about how a company is run, with modern organisational forms and strategies. The structuring options are diverse and require fresh ideas.

The "Digital Innovation Management" degree course guarantees both the connection to a young, international research discipline and a direct reference to current entrepreneurial challenges, and provides a direct insight into the current topics facing SMEs and world market leaders in the region.

The programme is specially designed to prepare students for a number of key positions in digitalisation in companies and also includes cross-cutting issues such as leading consulting projects, training in communication skills and a convincing line of argument.

data.headline: Admission requirements
data.text:
- completed university degree with 210 ECTS and grade 2.5 or better
- 15 ECTS from the field of IT Management, Information Technology (IT) and Business Administration (alternatively, oral examinations (each 30 minutes) can be taken at Neu-Ulm University of Applied Sciences)
- Proof of English language skills level B2 according to CEFR
- Proof of German language skills level A1 according to CEFR

data.text: ERP and Analytical Systems, IT Quality Management, Data Analysis, Design Thinking, Industry 4.0, Project Management, Quality-Driven Software Development, Requirement Engineering, SAP;, Test-Driven Development

data.headline: Target group
data.text: Current challenges of the industry consist in the digitisation and networking of operational processes from product development to logistics to intelligent production according to Industry 4.0 concepts. The high degree of complexity requires a sound knowledge of computer science and business administration. This is where our 3-semester Master's degree course "Informatics and Business" comes in. In addition to theoretical and practical specialisation in the two main areas of ‘ERP and Analytical Systems’ and ‘IT Quality Management’, the programme imparts knowledge of SAP®, software engineering, IT auditing, information management and data science at an international level.

data.headline: Annotation
data.text: In parallel, the degree in Industrial Engineering M.Sc. can be obtained, provided that the Bachelor's degree qualifying for admission comprises at least 10 credit points from the field of engineering.

data.headline: Admission requirements
data.text: A successfully completed Bachelor’s degree worth at least 210 ECTS in the following areas: a) Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration or International Business Administration at South Westphalia University of Applied Sciences, b) Bachelor’s degree in Business Information Systems, c) Bachelor’s degree in Business Information Systems with at least 20 ECTS credits in Business Administration content, d) Bachelor’s degree in Industrial Engineering with at least 20 ECTS credits in Computer Science content, e) Bachelor’s degree covering a range of subjects including Business Administration, Computer Science and cross-sectional subjects (e.g. Mathematics, Statistics, Languages, Social Skills). Applicants will only be admitted if they have completed their studies with a) a final grade of 2.0 or better or b) a final grade of at least 2.5 and a thesis with a grade of 1.7 or better.

data.headline: Admission requirements
data.text:
Admission to the Master's degree course in Artificial Intelligence can be granted to those who have very good or good knowledge and skills in the field of computer science and/or mathematics, demonstrated by a relevant, practice-oriented, scientifically based qualification.

The qualification is demonstrated by a completed certificate of academic degree with 210 credit points according to the European Credit Transfer and Accumulation System (ECTS, hereinafter referred to as ECTS credits) and an overall grade of 2.5 or better in the areas of Computer Science, Mathematics or a related degree course at a German university or an equivalent degree.
Each qualification must be assessed individually, depending on the educational background of the individual student.

data.headline: Target group
data.text:
To address the shortage of professionally qualified
specialists in this area of IoT, the University of Applied
Science Nordhausen introduces a new full-time Master's programme
computer Engineering for IoT Systems.
The programme provides an introduction to the disciplines
that are part of typical IoT solutions such as
Microelectronics, Cloud Computing, Embedded Software,
Wireless Networking, Data Science and Artificial
Intelligence. The programme emphasises the relations of
these disciplines and shows ways to combine them for a
complete solution. The wide range of involved disciplines
makes it an academically challenging programme.

data.headline: Admission requirements
data.text:
Entry requirements
• Bachelor‘s degree in Computer Engineering or similar fields
• US-GPA above 3.3 (is equal to German grading system 2.5 or less)
• English proficiency (TOEFL iBT 79, IELTS 6.0 or completed Bachelor‘s programme in English)
• APS (students from China and Vietnam)

(1) Admission requirements to the Master's degree programme in Computer Engineering for IoT Systems is proof of a first certificate of academic degree in a degree course in computer science or computer science related to at least three years with the Bachelor’s academic degree in Engineering (B.Eng.) or a professionally comparable professionally qualifying certificate of academic degree.

data.headline: Focus
data.text: Supply Chain Management, Process Management, Programming, Business Intelligence, Big Data, Operations Research, Enterprise Resource Planning, Digital Transformation, International Management

data.headline: Target group
data.text: Graduates with a first certificate of academic degree in Logistics, Industrial Engineering, Economics, Engineering, Information Technology or related disciplines,

data.headline: Annotation
data.text:
Initial start: Winter semester 2023/24

The digitisation of the economy, geopolitical changes and increasing cost pressure are having enormous impacts on the logistics and supply chain industry. Companies are therefore constantly looking for experts who can deal with this digital transformation and gain insights from large amounts of data in order to develop innovative supply chain solutions and business strategies.

Take on these challenges and become part of a new generation of supply chain managers that knows how to deal with innovative digital solutions and complex SCM platforms and works confidently in a global and diverse environment.

In the degree course, you will get to know the most important supply chain concepts, digital tools and their application. You will learn more about Supply Chain Management 4.0, innovation management, process management and big data and will be versed in current topics such as business intelligence, digital transformation and operations research.

The use and customisation of SAP, the leading enterprise resource planning system, is just as familiar to you as programming apps. In addition, you will expand your knowledge of platform economics and digital business models and apply agile methods in study projects.

Thanks to the project and skill-based approach, you will also develop your leadership, communication and intercultural skills and are therefore optimally prepared for demanding and international positions in digital supply chain management.

data.headline: Admission requirements
data.text:
To apply for the Master’s degree programme in Digital Supply Chain Management, you will need:

- Academic degree (Bachelor's or Diploma degree) from a university or university of applied sciences (Bachelor's or Diploma degree) from a university or university of applied sciences in Logistics, Industrial Engineering, Economics, Engineering, Information Technology or related disciplines
– Letter of motivation
- Certificate of general or subject-specific higher education entrance qualification
- Proof of command of English
- Curriculum vitae with current passport photo
- Copy of identity document (front and back), copy of passport or national identity card for foreign students

data.text:
Completion of a university degree in Computer Science or a related subject at a German university or comparable university abroad. Successful proof of aptitude for the subject is provided in the form of an aptitude test conducted by the department.

head.title: Engineering and Management of Space Systems

items.name: Deadlines
items.text: Please enquire

data.headline: Focus
data.text: Space Technologies, Computer Science, Electronics Engineering

data.headline: Annotation
data.text:
The course of study offers an interdisciplinary degree course that links up with the engineering sciences in the fields of computer science, electrical engineering and mechanical engineering and combines them with overarching interdisciplinary system competencies. Oriented to the basic concept of systems engineering, students acquire technical know-how at the cutting edge of research and application skills for practical astronautics-related projects on concrete technical systems (e.g. satellite systems). Supplemented by management and social skills, the aim is to take the constantly increasing complexity of software-intensive technical systems in the space industry into account.
The degree course is designed as a strategic cooperation with the Gdańsk University of Technology. The study programme concept provides for one theoretical semester to be completed in Gdańsk and one in Bremen and for the credits earned to be credited to the curricula of the respective study programmes at both universities to enable students to obtain two degrees as a ‘double degree’.

data.headline: Focus
data.text: Automotive Computer Science, Software Engineering, Software-defined vehicle, Securecar, Autonomous driving, Driver Assistance Systems, Artificial Intelligence

data.headline: Target group
data.text: Graduates of Diploma degree and Bachelor’s degree course in the field of Computer Science, Electrical and Information Technology and related degree courses.

data.headline: Annotation
data.text: The automotive industry is one of the most important industries in Bavaria. In addition to large car and truck manufacturers, numerous supply companies are also located here. For the mobility of the future, more and more functions are being implemented via software in modern vehicles. In some cases, more than 200 control units are installed in a vehicle and up to 16 gigabytes of software data are imported. Software is therefore a crucial key component, which is why the industry is now talking about Software Defined Vehicles (SDV). This development requires highly complex systems with hardware and software components for more and more safety, comfort and entertainment on board, which in turn requires highly qualified experts for development and implementation.

data.headline: Admission requirements
data.text:
- Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Electrical and Information Technology or a related subject.
- Successful completion of recruitment test and selection interview.
- Language requirements
The admission is defined in the study and examination regulations (Section 5 Qualification and Entry Requirements as well as Admission).

data.headline: Focus
data.text: Safety and Security of Intelligent Systems, Explainable Robotics, Intelligent Manipulation, Machine Learning, Artificial Intelligence, Autonomous Systems, Intelligent Robots, Systems Engineering, Human Robot Interaction

data.headline: Annotation
data.text: The Master Program Autonomous Systems is offered by the Institute of Applied Sciences of the Bonn-Aachen International Center for Information Technology (b-it). This institute is based on the cooperation between two renowned German competence centres: the Fraunhofer Institute for Intelligent Analysis and Information Systems (IAIS) and the Department of Computer Science of the University of Bonn-Rhein-Sieg (H-BRS).

data.headline: Area of study
items: Partner institution: University of New Brunswick in Canada (International degree: Master of Science)

data.headline: Admission requirements
data.text:
First professionally qualifying university degree (Bachelor, Diplom or equivalent) in a computer science degree course or a mathematical-scientific, engineering or economics degree course with a sufficient computer science component.

Sufficient knowledge of concepts, methods and tools in the field of Computer Science. Applicants who have already completed their first degree course in mathematical/scientific subjects or mechanical engineering can be admitted if at least 50% of the computer science content has been taught. In this case, additional courses of up to 30 ECTS may be required.
Proof of the required English language skills.
No knowledge of the German language is required for this degree course.

data.text: Have you completed your bachelor's degree in Computer Science or a related field and are you now ready to advance your career? data.headline: Admission requirements
data.text:
You need to have a completed bachelor's degree with at least 180 credit points.
In your bachelor’s degree you must have gained at least 60 credit points in the fields of computer science, software engineering, information technology, or another field with at least 60 CP in computer science-related topics such as mathematics, programming, design, and software architecture.
Your English language skills must be equivalent to Level B2 of the European Framework of Reference for Languages (CEFR).

data.headline: Focus
data.text: Programming & Software Engineering, Machine Learning & Applied Statistics, Business Operations & Logistics, Digital Performance Marketing & Automation, Agile Project Management & Design Thinking, Artificial Intelligence & Deep Learning, Business Intelligence for Big Data & MLOps, Electives, IT Architectures, Cloud & IT Management, eCommerce, CRM & Lead Management

data.headline: Annotation
data.text:
Excellent career and salary prospects in Germany and worldwide. Most of our students receive job offers before they get their academic degree.

AI is revolutionizing and driving the new business era. Our graduates are sought-after experts who understand both the technology and the economic aspects. You will benefit from a strong and growing job market in Germany and a solid salary level.

This Executive Master's degree programme uniquely positions graduates at the interface between innovative IT and digital business management. Typical professions are Data Scientist, Business Analyst, AI Consultant, AI Project Manager, Digital Business Developer, Digital Business Consultant, E-Commerce Manager, Performance Marketing Manager and IT System Administrator.

Companies value our graduates because they can quickly make themselves useful with a wide range of applicable knowledge. The hybrid form of the lectures supports the flexibility and mobility of our students to accept a working student position and continue their studies wherever the company is located.

Our international students and graduates work in world-leading companies such as Accenture, EY, KPMG, PWC, Deloitte, IBM, HP, SAP, Oracle, Vodafone, eBay, Amazon, Lufthansa, TUI, Expedia, Trivago, Audi, Porsche, Mercedes-Benz, Hugo Boss, Bosch, Siemens, Aldi and Lidl.

Prof. Dr. Pavel Rawe, PhD
Dean of Studies International Business Information Systems (BSc.) (IBS)
Consultation hours: Appointment lists for booking office hours are posted on Prof. Rawe's office door - Building I, Room 2.09 No appointments are given online, by telephone or by email.

data.headline: Target group
data.text: Graduates of a bachelor's degree course or comparable, e.g. engineers, industrial engineers, business economists, computer scientists and graduates of related disciplines

data.headline: Annotation
data.text:
Why study Industrial Artificial Intelligence IAI?
The teaching language of the Industrial Artificial Intelligence degree programme is English.
IAI is for people who are interested in all aspects of artificial intelligence and want to play an active role in shaping the topic of artificial intelligence. You will effectively link the relevant industrial business areas with artificial intelligence, recognise efficiency potential and implement your findings in practical projects with companies. Learning by doing will lead you to success in this project-oriented degree programme.
AI technology is changing the world of work: ‘By 2030, around 30% of current working hours could be automated by technology, including generative AI’ (McKinsey Global Institute, 2025). All areas of companies will be affected, including production, logistics or supply chain, planning, purchasing, manufacturing or assembly and many more.
The degree opens up excellent career opportunities in the industry, as experts in artificial intelligence are sought-after graduates in a rapidly growing market for artificial intelligence: according to Statista (2024), the market volume will increase from USD 96 billion in 2021 to an estimated USD 1.848 billion in 2030.

What does the IAI Master’s programme look like?

The programme combines theory and practice within the framework of projects. Learning by doing is at the centre of the course. Different specialisations are taught in each semester:
- The Industrial Operation and Transformation specialisation deals with the relevant AI application areas and the associated, marketable AI tools that shape everyday practice
- The Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering specialisation provides in-depth knowledge that enables you to independently develop and refine AI tools and thus make an important contribution beyond the practical application of tools.

You will acquire comprehensive knowledge in AI-oriented Python programming, machine and deep learning as well as generative AI. You will also expand your knowledge of big data, data science and data engineering. This knowledge is supplemented by practical knowledge of application software packages from well-known manufacturers (e.g. Microsoft, SAP, Siemens, AWS), which deal with topics such as ERP systems, cloud computing, robotic process automation, business intelligence and analytics.

Semester structure / programme content

You will acquire comprehensive knowledge in AI-oriented Python programming, machine and deep learning as well as generative AI. You will also expand your knowledge of big data, data science and data engineering. This knowledge is supplemented by practical knowledge of application software packages from well-known manufacturers (e.g. Microsoft, SAP, Siemens, AWS), which deal with topics such as ERP systems, cloud computing, robotic process automation, business intelligence and analytics.


Your future: What can you achieve with your degree?

With your degree, you will have a wide range of career opportunities, some of which we cannot even fully assess today. In addition to the traditional areas of employment / job offers, there are also new areas of employment for IAI Master’s graduates that are being created by AI in companies.

These include the following jobs:
- AI engineer – These are responsible for integrating artificial intelligence into existing industrial systems or developing it for these systems themselves.
- AI consultant – They carry out analyses and develop concepts for the introduction of AI technology and its application to increase costs and efficiency in industrial business areas.
- AI business developer – Develops and implements AI/ML models and solutions for specific business challenges.
- AI product manager – A specialist to oversee, create and manage products that utilise AI technologies.
- AI research scientist – A professional who conducts research and development in the field of artificial intelligence.

Machine Learning and Software Engineering: Theory and practical implementation of artificial intelligence methods. Graduates can select suitable algorithms, parameterise them and implement them in a usable application. In addition, they are able to generate an AI-compatible data set from predefined raw data by being able to safely apply suitable data analysis and processing methods.

Human Computer Interaction: In-depth understanding of user interface design. Graduates can design these ergonomically according to customer requirements.

data.headline: Admission requirements
data.text: The requirement for enrolment in the degree programme with vocational and academic elements, which is taught in English, is a contract with a company that, in addition to the basic cooperation agreement with the university, provides assurance that the business language used in the company is English. This company must be found independently by the applicant. The Kaiserslautern University of Applied Sciences’ company database provides guidance on this.

data.headline: Target group
data.text: Graduates of Computer Science or degree courses with a Computer Science component of at least 70%.

data.headline: Annotation
data.text:
High-integrity systems are complex, software-controlled systems. These systems protect people, the environment, organisations and society. They can be divided into two areas of application:
- Safety-critical systems (SCS) have a direct impact on the life and health of humans and the environment. They are used in all industrial sectors, e.g. aerospace, automotive, railway and marine systems, power generation, medical technology, SCADA and others.
- Mission-critical systems (MCS) have a high criticality with regard to the functioning of an organization, e.g. ERP, CRM and others.

A Master's academic degree in High Integrity Systems opens up access to a wide range of professional opportunities in various areas of application in computer science. The development of software and IT services for high integrity systems is crucial for all industries, as well as administrative applications, banking and financial systems.

data.headline: Admission requirements
data.text:
Admission requirements:
- The Bachelor's or Diploma examination in a university degree course of at least six semesters worth a minimum of 180 ECTS credit points in Computer Science or in another degree course in which Computer Science accounts for at least 70 % of the ECTS credit points possible in this degree course. The grade of the certificate of academic degree must be at least 1.8. Applicants with a Bachelor's grade between 1.9 and 2.5 can be admitted as part of a special procedure if they can prove they have special qualifications.
-English proficiency level B2 through a language test of the CEFR, not older than 3 years (e.g. TOEFL, IELTS, Cambridge Certificate, DAAD)
- Curriculum Vitae
-Letter of motivation
Further information can be found on the website of the degree course:
https://www.frankfurt-university.de/de/studium/master-studiengange/high-integrity-systems-msc/fuer-studieninteressierte/
